es.summary: Recién nacido entre las 37 semanas y antes de cumplir las 42 semanas de gestación (37 0/7 a 41 6/7). Es el rango esperado y el de menor riesgo.
key_points: Término: desde las 37 semanas hasta antes de las 42 semanas de gestación.
Antes de 37 semanas es pretérmino (RNP); desde las 42 semanas, postérmino (RN post).
La combinación más frecuente en las notas es RNTAEG: término y adecuado para la edad gestacional.
Un RNT AEG suele pesar entre 2 500 y 4 000 g.

usage: Ejemplo: «RNTAEG femenino, 39 semanas por FUR, peso 3 300 g, Apgar 9/9».
La edad gestacional se confirma tras el nacimiento con Ballard o Capurro.
nursing_care: Realizar la valoración inmediata (Apgar) y el examen físico completo.
Graficar peso, talla y perímetro cefálico para clasificar en PEG, AEG o GEG.
Favorecer el alojamiento conjunto y la lactancia materna exclusiva.

en.summary: A newborn born from 37 weeks up to before 42 weeks of gestation (37 0/7 to 41 6/7; RNT in Spanish). This is the expected range with the lowest risk.
key_points: Full term: from 37 weeks up to before 42 weeks of gestation.
Before 37 weeks is preterm (RNP); from 42 weeks it is postterm (RN post).
The most common combination in notes is RNTAEG: term and appropriate for gestational age.
A term AGA newborn usually weighs between 2,500 and 4,000 grams.

usage: Example: "RNTAEG female, 39 weeks by LMP, weight 3,300 g, Apgar 9/9".
Gestational age is confirmed after birth with the Ballard or Capurro score.
nursing_care: Perform the immediate assessment (Apgar) and a full physical exam.
Plot weight, length and head circumference to classify as SGA, AGA or LGA.

key_points.1.quote: Premature (less than 37 weeks gestation) Full term (37 to 42 weeks gestation) Post term (born after 42 weeks gestation)

key_points.3.quote: The weight for full-term infants that are born AGA will most often be between 2,500 grams (about 5.5 pounds [lbs] or 2.5 kilograms [kg]) and 4,000 grams (about 8.8 lbs or 4 kg).

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: After birth, gestational age can be measured by looking at the baby's weight, length, head circumference , vital signs, reflexes , muscle tone, posture, and the condition of the skin and hair.
